exposure: Virtual antenatal care trajectories (low and stable virtual care, high first trimester virtual care, high second trimester virtual care, high third trimester virtual care)
cohort: The study included 34,114 mother-child dyads from a multiethnic and socioeconomically deprived UK inner-city population observed between October 2018 and July 2023.
finding: A higher proportion of virtual antenatal care contacts during the second or third trimesters was associated with an increased risk of several adverse pregnancy outcomes.
mod_finding: High second trimester virtual care was associated with less assisted vaginal birth and more labor induction, while high third trimester virtual care was linked to more elective or emergency cesarean sections and fewer third-degree/fourth-degree vaginal tears.
gest_age: Gestational age was used to define antenatal care windows (0 to >=37 weeks) and premature birth (<37 weeks) was an outcome.
